regions.name: The Rimeward Range
regions.terrain: mountain, ice and bare rock
regions.water: snowmelt streams; the head of the Rimewater
regions.notes: The north-west of the ice range. Passes closed in winter.

regions.name: The Varrun Heights
regions.terrain: mountain, ice, with passes
regions.water: snowmelt; the head of the Braidwater
regions.notes: The middle of the ice range, above the high plain. The holds of the Varrun. The front of the range above the Carrow Plain is a line of bare foothills with one gap.

regions.name: The Greystone Uplands
regions.terrain: mountain, bare grey stone
regions.water: springs out of rock; the head of the Tessen
regions.notes: Stony uplands of the north-east. Thinly peopled.

regions.name: The Shoreward Fells
regions.terrain: highland, stony hills falling to the east coast
regions.water: short becks to the sea and to Emmer Bay
regions.climate: cool upland, wetter on the sea side
regions.notes: Hills behind the east coast.

regions.name: The Orvan Steppe
regions.terrain: steppe, open grass under the range
regions.water: the Little Rime; snowmelt in spring
regions.notes: The winter country of the Orvanni.

regions.name: The Windrow Steppe
regions.terrain: steppe, open grass
regions.water: the upper Rimewater; the Windrow Brook
regions.notes: Open and godless. Herds cross it in summer.

regions.name: The Carrow Plain
regions.terrain: plain, high grassland with wet ground by the river
regions.water: the Braidwater, braided over gravel, high with melt in spring
regions.notes: River country opening onto high plain, under the foothills of the range.

regions.name: The Springfoot Vale
regions.terrain: valley, stony at its head, braided river below
regions.water: the Tessen, from springs, with fords
regions.notes: The upper Tessen under the Greystone Uplands.

regions.name: The Coldwater Coast
regions.terrain: coast, steppe margin and low shore
regions.water: the lower Rimewater; the Cold Sea
regions.notes: Thinly peopled shore of the west.

regions.name: The Threeways Hills
regions.terrain: hill, rough hill country
regions.water: short streams; the head of the Wodewater
regions.notes: Hill clans. The only hill country of the west.

regions.name: The Fordmeet Plain
regions.terrain: plain, where steppe, hills and river plain meet
regions.water: the upper Meld; the low divide to the Windrow Brook
regions.notes: The country of the three roads.

regions.name: The Westwood Marches
regions.terrain: forest, open woods and glades with grass between
regions.water: the Wodewater
regions.notes: Wood and grass west of the Threeways Hills. Open, few people.

regions.name: The Uncounted Wood
regions.terrain: forest, great old forest to the western shore
regions.water: forest streams
regions.notes: Deep forest. Wild. Beasts no one has counted.

regions.name: The Meldrin Vale
regions.terrain: plain, river plain and old fields
regions.water: the Meld; the Tessen and the Eastmeld join it here
regions.notes: The heart of the old kingdom of Meldrin.

regions.name: The Sleeper's Downs
regions.terrain: hill, one lone mass of bare brown downs
regions.water: no stream runs off it
regions.notes: Seen from any height the downs have the plain shape of a great beast lying asleep. The paint drew it some 350 miles long; the downs are the ground it shows, and the hoarder itself is the site inside it, at its true size.

regions.name: The Underlee Plain
regions.terrain: plain, open grass south and west of the downs
regions.water: the head of the Brindlewater
regions.notes: Open and godless.

regions.name: The Eastmeld Plain
regions.terrain: plain, river plain under the fells
regions.water: the Eastmeld; the Fellwater
regions.notes: The east of Meldrin.

regions.name: The Askeld Marches
regions.terrain: plain, grassland at the forest's edge
regions.water: the Brindlewater
regions.notes: Grass meeting forest, the river through it, hills behind.

regions.name: The Brindle Hills
regions.terrain: hill, low hills between the plain and the black soil
regions.water: springs on both sides
regions.notes: Hills behind the southern plain.

regions.name: The Sable Plain
regions.terrain: plain, black soil, thinly farmed
regions.water: the lower Brindlewater
regions.notes: The west of the black-soil plain.

regions.name: The Orren Plain
regions.terrain: plain, black-soil flood plain
regions.water: the Orrenwater, wide and slow, floods in spring
regions.notes: The east of the black-soil plain. Dyked fields.

regions.name: The Vessar Coast
regions.terrain: coast, low hills and coves along the south shore
regions.water: short rivers; the south sea
regions.notes: The south coast. The country of the Vessari.

regions.name: The Ilwemere
regions.terrain: marsh, reed delta of many channels
regions.water: the mouths of the Meld
regions.notes: Reed country. The waters of the Ilwe.

regions.name: The Tollwater Reach
regions.terrain: valley, wide slow river with marsh at its edges
regions.water: the lower Meld and the Bayward Arm, with fords
regions.notes: Ford towns, old tollhouses.

regions.name: The Saltgate Shore
regions.terrain: coast, shingle and salt pans under the fells
regions.water: Emmer Bay; the narrows to the sea
regions.notes: The north shore of Emmer Bay.

regions.name: The Hook of Emmer
regions.terrain: coast, a long low hook of land round the bay
regions.water: Emmer Bay within, the sea without
regions.notes: Few safe landings on its seaward side.

regions.name: The Cold Sea
regions.terrain: sea, cold and grey
regions.water: open sea
regions.notes: Off the north-west and the west.

regions.name: The Easting Sea
regions.terrain: sea, open
regions.water: open sea
regions.notes: Off the north-east and the east.

regions.name: The Sunward Sea
regions.terrain: sea, open
regions.water: open sea
regions.notes: Off the south.

regions.name: Emmer Bay
regions.terrain: sea, a great sheltered bay
regions.water: sheltered salt water; a narrow way to the Easting Sea by the Saltgate narrows
regions.notes: The paint closes the narrows; they are a few hundred yards wide at Saltgate, finer than a pixel.

features.name: The Braidwater
features.known_to: the Carrow; the Orvanni; the Fordfolk
features.notes: Braided over gravel bars across the high plain. Joins the Rimewater.

features.name: The River Meld
features.known_to: every people of the middle and east
features.notes: The longest river. Rises on the low divide of the Fordmeet Plain and runs east, then south-east to the Ilwemere.

features.name: The Windrow Brook
features.notes: Rises a few miles from the head of the Meld, across a low divide, and runs west to the Rimewater.

features.name: The River Tessen
features.notes: From stone springs in the Greystone Uplands, braided in its middle reaches, with fords. Joins the Meld.

aliases.name: the Reach
aliases.notes: The god's word for the whole water its people walk, the Tessen and the Meld below it; a way of speaking, not a place.

features.name: The Orrenwater
features.notes: The western arm of the Meld, wide and slow, along the edge of the black soil.

features.name: The Bayward Arm
features.notes: The eastern arm of the Meld, into the south-west corner of Emmer Bay.

features.name: The Orvan Beck
features.notes: A snowmelt stream off the range to the Little Rime. Finer than the paint shows; data only.

features.name: Carrowford Town
features.notes: The town the player named Carrowford; the map name carries one word more only because the tool does not let a player's own name for a place be the map name itself (it must be an alias by the player to count as heard). On a rise above the ford of the Braidwater, where the Old North Road comes down to the river. Wood and stone, a market, a granary, a wall of earth and timber.

features.name: Kes Orvan
features.notes: Named by god-storms. The winter town of the Orvanni on the Little Rime: low timber and sod halls.

features.name: The Highgrass Camp
features.notes: A great herd camp of the Orvanni, tents and wagon houses, under the range. Stands in spring; moves with the herds.

features.name: Threeways
features.notes: Named by god-roads. A market town at the ford of the Meld where three old roads cross.

features.name: Saltgate
features.notes: Named by god-sea. A walled harbor town on the narrows of Emmer Bay.

features.name: Kellgarth
features.notes: Named by god-beasts. A walled town on the grass at the forest's edge, by the Brindlewater.

features.name: Orrenmark
features.notes: Named by god-harvest. A walled town on the black plain at the ford of the Orrenwater.

features.name: Meldry
features.notes: The old seat of the kings of Meldrin, on the Meld. Larger than its people now fill.

features.name: Estbridge
features.notes: A Meldrin town at the bridge of the Eastmeld.

features.name: Tollford
features.notes: A ford town where the Meld parts into its arms. Meldrin in name.

features.name: Vessa
features.notes: The chief harbor town of the Vessari, on the south coast.

features.name: Varrunhold
features.notes: The chief hold of the Varrun, in the heights. Nearest listed type; a hold cut into a mountain side, not a town of streets.

features.name: Ilwenstead
features.notes: The largest gathering of the Ilwe: houses on piles in the reeds.

features.name: Reedham
features.notes: A ford village on the Bayward Arm where the Reedwain winter.

features.name: The Old North Road
features.notes: Old paved road of the fallen kingdom, from the gap in the foothills down to the ford at Carrowford and south across the plain to Threeways. The grass road of the Fordfolk.

features.name: The Hill Road
features.notes: Old paved road into the Threeways Hills.

features.name: The Meld Road
features.notes: Old paved road down the Meld. The river road of the Fordfolk.

features.name: The Toll Road
features.known_to: the Reedwain; the Quayfolk; the Meldrin
features.notes: Old paved road from Tollford past the ruined tollhouse and round the bay to Saltgate.

features.name: The Dry Road
features.notes: Old paved road down a dry older bed of the Tessen to Meldry.

features.name: The Wood Road
features.notes: Old paved road from Kellgarth north along the wood's edge to the Hill Road, two or three days west of Threeways.

features.name: The Bin Road
features.notes: Old road from Orrenmark through the Brindle Hills to Tollford.

features.name: The School Road
features.notes: Coast road from Vessa by the school to Orrenmark.

features.name: The Bank Track
features.notes: A worn track along the bank of the Braidwater.

features.name: The Varrun Gate
features.known_to: the Carrow, as the gap; the Varrun
features.notes: The one gap in the line of foothills above the Carrow Plain; the way up to the Varrun holds. Closed by snow in winter.

features.name: The Stane Door
features.known_to: the Varrun; a tale among the Carrow
features.notes: A sealed door in the hillside by the gap. The mouth of u01.

features.name: The Barrow Door
features.notes: A sealed door in a hill by the Hill Road. The mouth of u02.

features.name: The Door of Terms
features.known_to: the Reedwain, as a tale; the Orrenfolk
features.notes: A door in the Brindle Hills with terms cut on it. The mouth of u03.

features.name: The Fell Door
features.notes: A door in the Shoreward Fells. No one has found a lock on it. The mouth of u04.

features.name: The Capped Spring
features.notes: A spring capped with worked stone in the Greystone Uplands. The mouth of u07.

features.name: The Rime Bones
features.notes: Great bones in the ice of the Rimeward Range.

features.name: The Strand Bones
features.notes: Great bones on the east shore, washed up long ago.

features.name: The Long Mound
features.notes: A long mound the Wood Road runs over. Great bones lie under the road here.

features.name: The Worn Altar
features.notes: A half-sunk altar with its face worn off, at the edge of a field by the ford.

features.name: The Old Tollhouse
features.notes: A ruined tollhouse at the ford of the Bayward Arm, with ledgers no one reads.

features.name: The Dry Market
features.notes: A ruined market on the Meld Road.

features.name: The Roofless Hall
features.notes: A roofless hall on the steppe, the weather for its ceiling.

features.name: The Hollow Hall
features.notes: An empty hall on the black soil.

features.name: The Fallen Stone
features.notes: The warm blue-grey stone that fell on the night the gods came down. On the open steppe, in godless country between the seats of god-roads and god-storms, 70 hundredths of the way from the first (r-0144, r-0145). No people has named it.

features.name: The Sleeper's Brow
features.known_to: the Meldrin, who do not go up; herders
features.notes: The hoarder: the living thing at the head of the downs, under the star, at its true size, a few miles across. The center point.

features.name: The School at Ombrel
features.known_to: the Vessari; workers everywhere, by name
features.notes: The school of workers, on the south coast.

features.name: The First Ford
features.notes: The first ford of the Tessen, below the spring.

features.name: Orren Ford
features.notes: The ford of the Orrenwater at Orrenmark.

features.name: Reedbank Ford
features.notes: The ford of the Bayward Arm by the old tollhouse.

features.name: The Ledge Spring
features.notes: A spring out of a stone ledge: the head of the Tessen.

layers.name: The Hollows Below
layers.notes: Mostly solid rock. Hollows only, shallow (cellar depth to a few hundred feet). No regions of its own, no painting: a layer of a few hollows is not painted (house style, the map block). Written on Night 3a before any painting request, from the placement plan's proportions; each hollow was moved to its mouth's traced point at 3a.5.

features.name: The Stane Hall
features.notes: The hall behind the sealed door in the spur of hills by the gap. Depth: a few hundred feet into the hillside. Mouth: the sealed door, a surface site.

features.name: The Barrow Hall
features.notes: The hall behind the sealed door in the hill by the crossing of three ways. Mouth: the sealed door, a surface site.

features.name: The Hall of Terms
features.notes: The hall behind the door with terms cut on it, in the hills behind the lower river. Mouth: the door, a surface site.

features.name: The Fell Hall
features.notes: The hall behind the door not known to have a lock, in the hills behind the east coast. Mouth: the door, a surface site.

features.name: The Elder Granary
features.known_to: the town over it, as cellars only
features.notes: A granary far too large, older than the town over it, cellar depth and below. Mouth: under the southern town.

features.name: The Drowned Quay
features.known_to: the harbor's people, as a story
features.notes: The older harbor under the living one: drowned quays and vaults under the harbor floor and wall. Mouth: at the harbor wall's foot.

features.name: The Capstone Chamber
features.notes: A spring capped with worked stone, with its chamber below. Mouth: the cap, a surface site in the north-east uplands.
